# Code Review Best Practices 

## Approaches to Code Review 

Method 1 

* Total rewrite of code from initial protocol 
* Paired review of differences 

Method 2 

* Antagonist review – try to create data that will break the code (important for code that will be used routinely)


## {#slide22-id data-menu-title="Importance of testing" background-image="images/testing.jpg" background-size="contain" footer="false"}

## Approaches to Code Review 

:::{.nonincremental}
Method 1 

* Total rewrite of code from initial protocol 
* paired review of differences 

Method 2 

* Antagonist review – try to create data that will break the code (important for code that will be used routinely)

:::

Method 3 

* Review and comment on code 

## Questions To Ask When Peer-Reviewing Code 

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
1. What does this code do?
2. Does the code function as I expect it to?
3. Does this code fulfill regulatory requirements?

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
4. How can this code be made more:
  - understandable
  - reliable
  - future-proof
  - efficient
  - reusable

:::
:::::

## Top Tip! ⏳

Set a time or line-of-code limit per session, to prevent reviewing with tired eyes 

## Code Indentation & Leaving Room For Your Code to Breathe 

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "|1-2|4-5|7-13"

# NO indentation NO room to breathe 
group_A<-data|>filter(group=="A")|>select(name,height,weight,age)

# NO indentation YES room to breathe 
group_A <- data |> filter(group == "A") |> select(name, height, weight, age)

# YES indentation YES room to breathe 
group_A <- data |> 
  filter(group == "A") |> 
  select(name, 
         height, 
         weight, 
         age)
```

## Overwriting Objects 

When exploring and wrangling data, avoid overwriting (`data <- data |> `) the data object until you are certain your wrangling code works as expected 

* write, execute, and check your code without assigning it into an object 
* create intermediate objects (`data_grouped`, `data_filtered`, etc)
* AND THEN you can safely overwrite your data object 

## Clearing Objects from Your Workspace 

```{r}
#| echo: true
x <- 1 
y <- 2 
z <- 3 

# list objects in your environment 
ls()
```

## Clearing Objects from Your Workspace {transition="none"}

Remove individual objects from your environment with `rm()`

```{r}
#| echo: true 

# here removing x and y only 
rm(x, y)

ls()
```

## Clearing Objects from Your Workspace {transition="none"}

Clear your whole environment with the broom icon 🧹 or 

```{r}
#| echo: true

# remove all objects in your environment 
rm(list = ls())

ls() # nothing left! Environment is empty 
```
